chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from al-Humaydi ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from al-'Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The divorce of the terminally ill (patient of death) is not valid, but his marriage is valid.

key_terms.الْعَلِيلِ: The terminally ill / patient of death

ai.seo_question: Is a divorce valid if issued by a terminally ill person in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's chain in al-Istibsar clarifies the legal status of a terminally ill person (al-'alil), ruling that their divorce is invalid while their marriage remains binding. This distinction prevents the premature dissolution of marital ties during the critical period of final illness, ensuring stability until death or full recovery. It reflects the Shia juristic view that the 'alil' retains full capacity for marriage but lacks the full authority to divorce due to the uncertainty of their condition.
